title: Commercial Shipping – Who's Who
description: Test your understanding of the main parties involved in commercial shipping, including shipowners, ship managers, charterers, cargo interests, brokers, agents, insurers, surveyors and maritime lawyers.

questions.question: Which party has legal ownership of a merchant vessel?
questions.explanation: The shipowner is the legal owner of the vessel. The owner may operate the vessel directly or appoint a ship manager.

questions.question: Who is the consignee?
options: The company managing the vessel technically
The party insuring the ship's machinery
questions.explanation: The consignee is the party named to receive the cargo at its destination.

questions.question: Which party normally sends or presents cargo for transportation?
questions.explanation: The shipper is the party sending or presenting the cargo for carriage.

questions.question: What is the main role of a freight forwarder?
options: To coordinate cargo transportation and logistics
To own the vessels used in the transport chain
To navigate the vessel during the voyage
questions.explanation: A freight forwarder coordinates cargo movement and may arrange shipping, customs clearance, storage and inland transport.

questions.question: Which party hires the use of a vessel under a charterparty?
questions.explanation: A charterer hires the vessel for a voyage, a period of time or under a bareboat arrangement.

questions.question: Which responsibility most commonly belongs to a ship management company?
questions.explanation: A ship manager may handle technical operations, crewing, maintenance, purchasing, budgeting, safety and regulatory compliance.

questions.question: What is the main function of a ship broker?
options: To connect shipowners and charterers and assist with negotiations
To recruit seafarers for the vessel
questions.explanation: A ship broker acts as an intermediary between owners and charterers and helps negotiate freight rates, hire and charterparty terms.

questions.question: Which party normally arranges pilotage, towage, berth bookings and local port formalities?
questions.explanation: The port or ship agent represents the vessel locally and coordinates the practical requirements of the port call.

questions.question: Which type of insurance primarily covers physical damage to the vessel and its machinery?
questions.explanation: Hull and Machinery insurance generally covers physical loss of or damage to the insured ship, hull, equipment and machinery.

questions.question: Which organisation commonly covers liabilities such as cargo claims, pollution and crew injuries?
questions.explanation: Protection and Indemnity clubs provide liability cover for risks such as cargo claims, pollution, crew injury and certain fines.

questions.question: A company hires a vessel to carry one cargo from Brazil to Japan. Which charter arrangement is most likely?
questions.explanation: A voyage charter is used when a vessel is hired for one specified voyage between agreed loading and discharge ports.

questions.question: A company hires a vessel for twelve months, directs its commercial employment and normally pays for bunkers and port charges. Which role does the company have?
questions.explanation: A time charterer hires the vessel for a specified period and normally controls its commercial employment while paying voyage-related expenses.

questions.question: A company takes over a vessel without crew and assumes responsibility for crewing and operation. Which arrangement does this describe?
questions.explanation: Under a bareboat charter, the charterer receives the vessel without crew and assumes extensive operational responsibilities.

questions.question: A shipowner appoints another company to handle maintenance, budgeting, dry-dock planning and regulatory compliance. Which party has been appointed?
questions.explanation: A ship manager may operate and maintain the vessel on behalf of the owner, including technical, financial and regulatory duties.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a shipowner from a ship manager?
options: The owner legally owns the vessel, while the manager may operate it on the owner's behalf.
The manager owns the vessel, while the owner only supplies the crew.
The owner handles port bookings, while the manager owns the cargo.
The manager provides marine insurance, while the owner acts as surveyor.
questions.explanation: Ownership and management are separate functions. The owner retains legal ownership, while the manager may carry out day-to-day operations.

questions.question: A container shipping line needs a local representative to handle bookings, customer service and bills of lading. Which party should it appoint?
questions.explanation: A liner agent represents a shipping line and may manage bookings, customer relations, cargo documentation and local port coordination.

questions.question: A shipping company needs to recruit officers and ratings, verify certificates and arrange crew travel. Which party would normally assist?
questions.explanation: A crewing agent recruits seafarers and may arrange employment contracts, travel, certification and training.

questions.question: After cargo damage, an independent specialist is appointed to inspect the goods and issue a factual condition report. Who is this?
questions.explanation: A marine or cargo surveyor inspects ships or cargo and reports on condition, damage, quantity, quality or compliance.

questions.question: A dispute concerns charterparty wording, cargo liability, salvage and general average. Which specialist is most likely to advise the parties?
questions.explanation: Maritime lawyers advise on shipping law, including charterparties, cargo claims, collisions, salvage, insurance and general average.

questions.question: A company buys grain internationally, sells it to overseas customers and charters vessels to transport it. Which commercial role best describes the company?
questions.explanation: A trader buys and sells commodities and may arrange shipping services to move them between markets.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a ship broker from a freight forwarder?
options: A ship broker mainly negotiates vessel employment, while a freight forwarder coordinates cargo logistics.
A freight forwarder owns the vessel, while a broker owns the cargo.
A broker performs vessel surveys, while a forwarder provides insurance.
A freight forwarder manages the crew, while a broker manages the engine room.
questions.explanation: A ship broker focuses on chartering and vessel employment. A freight forwarder focuses on coordinating the movement of cargo through the logistics chain.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes Hull and Machinery insurance from P&I insurance?
options: H&M covers physical damage to the vessel, while P&I covers third-party liabilities.
H&M covers only cargo claims, while P&I covers machinery repairs.
H&M covers crew recruitment, while P&I covers port agency services.
H&M covers freight rates, while P&I covers charter hire.
questions.explanation: Hull and Machinery insurance covers physical damage to the ship, while P&I covers liabilities involving third parties, cargo, pollution and crew.

questions.question: Which sequence most accurately represents a simple cargo movement?
questions.explanation: In a simplified transport chain, the shipper sends the cargo, the carrier transports it and the consignee receives it.

questions.question: A trader charters a vessel through a broker, while a ship manager operates the vessel and a port agent arranges the port call. Which statement is correct?
options: Each party performs a different contractual and operational role.
The broker becomes the legal owner of the vessel.
The port agent becomes responsible for all technical maintenance.
The ship manager automatically owns the cargo.
questions.explanation: Commercial shipping depends on several independent parties, each performing a specialised role under separate contractual arrangements.
